outcomes: A workspace chooses its task, change-proposal, memory and missions providers independently, in one place, and changing one never changes another
A user and a script call the same operation with the same request and read the same envelope, whether they type the command or call it over the extension host channel
A contract nobody bound and a capability the provider lacks are refused before anything runs, never reported as done
nonGoals: Choosing a provider when the workspace binds none, or substituting another backend when the bound one fails
Retrying a provider call on the caller's behalf
Promising atomicity, exclusivity or merge support a provider does not enforce
Implementing a hosted backend: providers are extensions, and the local one records tasks and proposals without hosted checks or merge
Authorizing merges, deployments or any mutation the caller is not already allowed to make

requirements.text: A workspace binds each contract in options.collaboration of putnami.workspace.json and nowhere else: one provider extension and one version. An unbound contract is unsupported (binding.missing), naming the block to add and the installed providers, none selected. A block that repeats a member is refused as binding.ambiguous. A provider that is absent, disabled or unprepared at its locked release is unavailable (binding.provider_missing) on either entry path. No failure is retryable or starts the provider.

capabilities reports, without running the provider, the binding status, the provider, and each operation of the bound version with required, supported, preconditions, description and hostOnly when set. A binding to an unknown version, or to a provider that lacks a required operation or breaks the contract, is invalid.

putnami <contract> <operation> --input and the host call collaboration.call share one route: the request is validated and normalized, a missing page to page.size 20, then sent through the extension tool transport to the one tool the bound provider declares, with the binding settings and, for selection operations, the resolved selection. Both return the same envelope; the command exits 0 only for ok. Provider tools never appear under their own names, and a workspace that binds nothing reserves no name.

An operation the catalog marks host-only is one the host that runs an agent calls, never the agent. putnami <contract> <operation> and the host channel's collaboration.call route it like any other operation, to the same envelope, and <contract>.capabilities marks it hostOnly.

No contract takes the name of a built-in command, command path or reserved alias, so putnami <contract> <operation> always reaches the collaboration route and discovers the installed extensions first.
